The sūtra prescribes दीर्घ (a class: ā ī ū ṝ …) for a vowel; with 1.2.28 the long vowel nearest to the sthānin by place is chosen — 1.1.50 (Kāśikā on 1.1.50: a+a gives the kaṇṭhya long ā).

why.txt: the substitute stands in the 1st case — Mahābhāṣya on 1.1.57: “आदेशः प्रथमानिर्दिष्टः”
दीर्घ is taught by its own name, so it falls only on a vowel (अचः) — काशिका on 1.2.28: “ह्रस्वदीर्घप्लुताः स्वसंज्ञया शिष्यमाणा अच एव स्थाने वेदितव्याः”

Where a rule teaches a substitute, a 6th-case word whose link is otherwise unclear names what is replaced (“… स्थाने”). Not in augment rules (the 6th is the host), not where another word names the part replaced (उपधायाः, एचः), not where no substitute is taught. (Bhāṣya: “सन्देहे नियमः।”)

Where a rule teaches a substitute, a 6th-case word whose link is otherwise unclear names what is replaced (“… स्थाने”). Not in augment rules (the 6th is the host), not where another word names the part replaced (उपधायाः, एचः), not where no substitute is taught. (Bhāṣya: “सन्देहे नियमः।”)
a suffix named in a rule stands for the word that ENDS in that suffix (starting from what it was added to) — ष्यङन्तस्य — what ENDS in it, as the Siddhānta-kaumudī reads it

A 7th-case word naming a following sound, suffix or word (“… परे”) puts the operation on what comes immediately before it. Not a 7th naming a meaning or domain (आर्धधातुके as ‘in its sphere’); if the rule also has a 5th, the 5th wins. (Bhāṣya: “शब्दे सप्तम्या निर्दिष्टे पूर्वस्य कार्यं यथा स्यात्। अर्थे मा भूत्।”)

why.txt: runs on from 6.1.13 (anuvṛtti)

Where a rule teaches a substitute, a 6th-case word whose link is otherwise unclear names what is replaced (“… स्थाने”). Not in augment rules (the 6th is the host), not where another word names the part replaced (उपधायाः, एचः), not where no substitute is taught. (Bhāṣya: “सन्देहे नियमः।”)

A 7th-case word naming a following sound, suffix or word (“… परे”) puts the operation on what comes immediately before it. Not a 7th naming a meaning or domain (आर्धधातुके as ‘in its sphere’); if the rule also has a 5th, the 5th wins. (Bhāṣya: “शब्दे सप्तम्या निर्दिष्टे पूर्वस्य कार्यं यथा स्यात्। अर्थे मा भूत्।”)

why.txt: the substitute stands in the 1st case — Mahābhāṣya on 1.1.57: “आदेशः प्रथमानिर्दिष्टः”

Where a rule teaches a substitute, a 6th-case word whose link is otherwise unclear names what is replaced (“… स्थाने”). Not in augment rules (the 6th is the host), not where another word names the part replaced (उपधायाः, एचः), not where no substitute is taught. (Bhāṣya: “सन्देहे नियमः।”)

A 7th-case word naming a following sound, suffix or word (“… परे”) puts the operation on what comes immediately before it. Not a 7th naming a meaning or domain (आर्धधातुके as ‘in its sphere’); if the rule also has a 5th, the 5th wins. (Bhāṣya: “शब्दे सप्तम्या निर्दिष्टे पूर्वस्य कार्यं यथा स्यात्। अर्थे मा भूत्।”)

why.txt: Where a rule teaches a substitute, a 6th-case word whose link is otherwise unclear names what is replaced (“… स्थाने”). Not in augment rules (the 6th is the host), not where another word names the part replaced (उपधायाः, एचः), not where no substitute is taught. (Bhāṣya: “सन्देहे नियमः।”)

A 7th-case word naming a following sound, suffix or word (“… परे”) puts the operation on what comes immediately before it. Not a 7th naming a meaning or domain (आर्धधातुके as ‘in its sphere’); if the rule also has a 5th, the 5th wins. (Bhāṣya: “शब्दे सप्तम्या निर्दिष्टे पूर्वस्य कार्यं यथा स्यात्। अर्थे मा भूत्।”)
By paribhāṣā 1.1.66, the locative 'samprasāraṇe' indicates that the prohibition applies to the preceding element.

A 5th-case word of direction (‘after X’) puts the operation on what comes immediately after it — something already there (substitute, augment, elision, accent). Placing a new suffix is 3.1.2; a 5th of cause or ‘other than’, or an explicit पूर्व, is not this rule. (Kāśikā: “पञ्चम्यर्थनिर्देश उत्तरस्यैव कार्यं भवति”)
runs on from 6.1.41 (anuvṛtti)

A 7th-case word naming a following sound, suffix or word (“… परे”) puts the operation on what comes immediately before it. Not a 7th naming a meaning or domain (आर्धधातुके as ‘in its sphere’); if the rule also has a 5th, the 5th wins. (Bhāṣya: “शब्दे सप्तम्या निर्दिष्टे पूर्वस्य कार्यं यथा स्यात्। अर्थे मा भूत्।”)

विभाषा names ‘not’ and ‘optionally’ together, so the rule's operation is optional; वा and अन्यतरस्याम् work the same way. A carried option word counts only where it is still in force (the commentary may call a rule nitya). बहुलम् is wider than an option. (Kāśikā: “विभाषाधिकारेऽपि नित्यसमास एवायम्।”)

why.txt: A vowel with त् after it stands only for vowels of its own length: अत् = short अ, आत् = long आ, एत्/ओत् = two-mora ए/ओ, not pluta. A vowel with त् after it stands only for vowels of its own length: अत् = short अ, आत् = long आ, एत्/ओत् = two-mora ए/ओ, not pluta. Check it is a real tapara: आत् may be the 5th case of अ (आद्गुणः), and a त् may belong to the form. (Kāśikā: “तपरो वर्णस्तत्कालस्यात्मना तुल्यकालस्य … ग्राहको भवति”)

An element marked with म् (नुम्, मुम्, श्नम्, अम्) goes right after the last vowel of what it is added to and becomes its final part. It replaces nothing: it overrides both the ‘in place of’ reading and the rule that a suffix follows. (Kāśikā: “अचां संनिविष्टानामन्त्यादचः परो मिद् भवति।”)

Where a rule teaches a substitute, a 6th-case word whose link is otherwise unclear names what is replaced (“… स्थाने”). Not in augment rules (the 6th is the host), not where another word names the part replaced (उपधायाः, एचः), not where no substitute is taught. (Bhāṣya: “सन्देहे नियमः।”)

A 7th-case word naming a following sound, suffix or word (“… परे”) puts the operation on what comes immediately before it. Not a 7th naming a meaning or domain (आर्धधातुके as ‘in its sphere’); if the rule also has a 5th, the 5th wins. (Bhāṣya: “शब्दे सप्तम्या निर्दिष्टे पूर्वस्य कार्यं यथा स्यात्। अर्थे मा भूत्।”)

a SOUND (a letter, a pratyāhāra, or the augment इट् — not a suffix or a word) in the 7th case, qualifying a 7th-case condition, stands for what BEGINS with it — so we read “…-आदि” (an exception to tadanta-vidhi, 1.1.72)

teaching_view.kind: एकादेशः — one substitute for two sounds

why.txt: the substitute stands in the 1st case — Mahābhāṣya on 1.1.57: “आदेशः प्रथमानिर्दिष्टः”
runs on from 6.1.84 (anuvṛtti)

Where a rule teaches a substitute, a 6th-case word whose link is otherwise unclear names what is replaced (“… स्थाने”). Not in augment rules (the 6th is the host), not where another word names the part replaced (उपधायाः, एचः), not where no substitute is taught. (Bhāṣya: “सन्देहे नियमः।”)

A 5th-case word of direction (‘after X’) puts the operation on what comes immediately after it — something already there (substitute, augment, elision, accent). Placing a new suffix is 3.1.2; a 5th of cause or ‘other than’, or an explicit पूर्व, is not this rule. (Kāśikā: “पञ्चम्यर्थनिर्देश उत्तरस्यैव कार्यं भवति”)

An अण् (vowels, semivowels, ह) or an उदित् (कु = the k-class) in a rule also stands for its savarṇas: उ = उवर्ण, short, long and pluta. Not when that sound is itself what the rule introduces, and not when त् follows it — then only 1.1.70. (Kaumudī: “अविधीयमानोऽण् उदिच्च सवर्णस्य संज्ञा स्यात्”)

teaching_view.kind: एकादेशः — one substitute for two sounds

why.txt: runs on from 6.1.88 (anuvṛtti)
runs on from 6.1.84 (anuvṛtti)

Where a rule teaches a substitute, a 6th-case word whose link is otherwise unclear names what is replaced (“… स्थाने”). Not in augment rules (the 6th is the host), not where another word names the part replaced (उपधायाः, एचः), not where no substitute is taught. (Bhāṣya: “सन्देहे नियमः।”)

A 5th-case word of direction (‘after X’) puts the operation on what comes immediately after it — something already there (substitute, augment, elision, accent). Placing a new suffix is 3.1.2; a 5th of cause or ‘other than’, or an explicit पूर्व, is not this rule. (Kāśikā: “पञ्चम्यर्थनिर्देश उत्तरस्यैव कार्यं भवति”)

a qualifier (viśeṣaṇa), agreeing with the word it qualifies (viśeṣya), stands for whatever ENDS in it — so we read “…-अन्त”; only the qualifier, never the qualified word (Nyāsa: “विशेषणेन चतदन्तविधिः [= च तदन्तविधिः], न विशेष्येण”)

Where a rule teaches a substitute, a 6th-case word whose link is otherwise unclear names what is replaced (“… स्थाने”). Not in augment rules (the 6th is the host), not where another word names the part replaced (उपधायाः, एचः), not where no substitute is taught. (Bhāṣya: “सन्देहे नियमः।”)

A 5th-case word of direction (‘after X’) puts the operation on what comes immediately after it — something already there (substitute, augment, elision, accent). Placing a new suffix is 3.1.2; a 5th of cause or ‘other than’, or an explicit पूर्व, is not this rule. (Kāśikā: “पञ्चम्यर्थनिर्देश उत्तरस्यैव कार्यं भवति”)

why.txt: the substitute stands in the 1st case — Mahābhāṣya on 1.1.57: “आदेशः प्रथमानिर्दिष्टः”
दीर्घ is taught by its own name, so it falls only on a vowel (अचः) — काशिका on 1.2.28: “ह्रस्वदीर्घप्लुताः स्वसंज्ञया शिष्यमाणा अच एव स्थाने वेदितव्याः”
runs on from 6.1.84 (anuvṛtti)

Where a rule teaches a substitute, a 6th-case word whose link is otherwise unclear names what is replaced (“… स्थाने”). Not in augment rules (the 6th is the host), not where another word names the part replaced (उपधायाः, एचः), not where no substitute is taught. (Bhāṣya: “सन्देहे नियमः।”)

A 5th-case word of direction (‘after X’) puts the operation on what comes immediately after it — something already there (substitute, augment, elision, accent). Placing a new suffix is 3.1.2; a 5th of cause or ‘other than’, or an explicit पूर्व, is not this rule. (Kāśikā: “पञ्चम्यर्थनिर्देश उत्तरस्यैव कार्यं भवति”)

a word in the 6th case in a rule names WHAT IS REPLACED — so we read “… स्थाने” — names the place — both sounds are replaced (“स्थाने”)

A 5th-case word of direction (‘after X’) puts the operation on what comes immediately after it — something already there (substitute, augment, elision, accent). Placing a new suffix is 3.1.2; a 5th of cause or ‘other than’, or an explicit पूर्व, is not this rule. (Kāśikā: “पञ्चम्यर्थनिर्देश उत्तरस्यैव कार्यं भवति”)

An अण् (vowels, semivowels, ह) or an उदित् (कु = the k-class) in a rule also stands for its savarṇas: उ = उवर्ण, short, long and pluta. Not when that sound is itself what the rule introduces, and not when त् follows it — then only 1.1.70. (Kaumudī: “अविधीयमानोऽण् उदिच्च सवर्णस्य संज्ञा स्यात्”)

A 5th-case word of direction (‘after X’) puts the operation on what comes immediately after it — something already there (substitute, augment, elision, accent). runs on from 6.1.113 (anuvṛtti)

Where a rule teaches a substitute, a 6th-case word whose link is otherwise unclear names what is replaced (“… स्थाने”). Not in augment rules (the 6th is the host), not where another word names the part replaced (उपधायाः, एचः), not where no substitute is taught. (Bhāṣya: “सन्देहे नियमः।”)
runs on from 6.1.113 (anuvṛtti)

A 5th-case word of direction (‘after X’) puts the operation on what comes immediately after it — something already there (substitute, augment, elision, accent). Placing a new suffix is 3.1.2; a 5th of cause or ‘other than’, or an explicit पूर्व, is not this rule. (Kāśikā: “पञ्चम्यर्थनिर्देश उत्तरस्यैव कार्यं भवति”)

A 7th-case word naming a following sound, suffix or word (“… परे”) puts the operation on what comes immediately before it. Not a 7th naming a meaning or domain (आर्धधातुके as ‘in its sphere’); if the rule also has a 5th, the 5th wins. (Bhāṣya: “शब्दे सप्तम्या निर्दिष्टे पूर्वस्य कार्यं यथा स्यात्। अर्थे मा भूत्।”)
runs on from 6.1.113 (anuvṛtti)

When one sound is taught in place of a longer item named in the 6th case, it replaces only that item's last sound. Not when the place is itself one sound or a position (उपधा, टि), not for augments, and not for लुक् — the whole suffix goes. (Nyāsa: “आदेशः पुनरत्रैकाल्लभ्यते।”)

Where a rule teaches a substitute, a 6th-case word whose link is otherwise unclear names what is replaced (“… स्थाने”). Not in augment rules (the 6th is the host), not where another word names the part replaced (उपधायाः, एचः), not where no substitute is taught. (Bhāṣya: “सन्देहे नियमः।”)

A 5th-case word of direction (‘after X’) puts the operation on what comes immediately after it — something already there (substitute, augment, elision, accent). a टित् augment goes at the BEGINNING, a कित् one at the END — it goes at the BEGINNING of the place

A 5th-case word of direction (‘after X’) puts the operation on what comes immediately after it — something already there (substitute, augment, elision, accent). Placing a new suffix is 3.1.2; a 5th of cause or ‘other than’, or an explicit पूर्व, is not this rule. (Kāśikā: “पञ्चम्यर्थनिर्देश उत्तरस्यैव कार्यं भवति”)
runs on from 6.1.140 (anuvṛtti)

A 7th-case word naming a following sound, suffix or word (“… परे”) puts the operation on what comes immediately before it. Not a 7th naming a meaning or domain (आर्धधातुके as ‘in its sphere’); if the rule also has a 5th, the 5th wins. (Bhāṣya: “शब्दे सप्तम्या निर्दिष्टे पूर्वस्य कार्यं यथा स्यात्। अर्थे मा भूत्।”)
a 7th-case word naming the setting — “in X” (not “when X follows”)

why.txt: runs on from 6.1.72 (anuvṛtti)
runs on from 6.1.135 (anuvṛtti)

A 5th-case word of direction (‘after X’) puts the operation on what comes immediately after it — something already there (substitute, augment, elision, accent). Placing a new suffix is 3.1.2; a 5th of cause or ‘other than’, or an explicit पूर्व, is not this rule. (Kāśikā: “पञ्चम्यर्थनिर्देश उत्तरस्यैव कार्यं भवति”)
चन्द्र here means the word चन्द्र itself, not its meaning or its synonyms — काशिका on 1.1.68: “शास्त्रे स्वमेव रूपं शब्दस्य ग्राह्यं बोध्यं प्रत्याय्यं भवति, न बाह्योऽर्थः”

A suffix named as a known element stands for the word from the base it was added to up to that suffix (सन् → सन्नन्त). Not in saṃjñā rules or the uttarapada section, nor when the rule teaches or changes that suffix; as a 7th-case condition it means ‘what begins with it’. (Śekhara: “संज्ञाविधौ … तदन्तग्रहणं नास्ति”)

A 5th-case word of direction (‘after X’) puts the operation on what comes immediately after it — something already there (substitute, augment, elision, accent). Placing a new suffix is 3.1.2; a 5th of cause or ‘other than’, or an explicit पूर्व, is not this rule. (Kāśikā: “पञ्चम्यर्थनिर्देश उत्तरस्यैव कार्यं भवति”)

why.txt: A 7th-case word naming a following sound, suffix or word (“… परे”) puts the operation on what comes immediately before it. A suffix named as a known element stands for the word from the base it was added to up to that suffix (सन् → सन्नन्त). A 7th-case word naming a following sound, suffix or word (“… परे”) puts the operation on what comes immediately before it. Not a 7th naming a meaning or domain (आर्धधातुके as ‘in its sphere’); if the rule also has a 5th, the 5th wins. (Bhāṣya: “शब्दे सप्तम्या निर्दिष्टे पूर्वस्य कार्यं यथा स्यात्। अर्थे मा भूत्।”)

runs on from 6.2.1 (anuvṛtti)

A 7th-case word naming a following sound, suffix or word (“… परे”) puts the operation on what comes immediately before it. Not a 7th naming a meaning or domain (आर्धधातुके as ‘in its sphere’); if the rule also has a 5th, the 5th wins. (Bhāṣya: “शब्दे सप्तम्या निर्दिष्टे पूर्वस्य कार्यं यथा स्यात्। अर्थे मा भूत्।”)
अध्यक्ष here means the word अध्यक्ष itself, not its meaning or its synonyms — काशिका on 1.1.68: “शास्त्रे स्वमेव रूपं शब्दस्य ग्राह्यं बोध्यं प्रत्याय्यं भवति, न बाह्योऽर्थः”
runs on from 6.2.64 (anuvṛtti)

विभाषा names ‘not’ and ‘optionally’ together, so the rule's operation is optional; वा and अन्यतरस्याम् work the same way. A carried option word counts only where it is still in force (the commentary may call a rule nitya). बहुलम् is wider than an option. (Kāśikā: “विभाषाधिकारेऽपि नित्यसमास एवायम्।”)

A 7th-case word naming a following sound, suffix or word (“… परे”) puts the operation on what comes immediately before it. Not a 7th naming a meaning or domain (आर्धधातुके as ‘in its sphere’); if the rule also has a 5th, the 5th wins. (Bhāṣya: “शब्दे सप्तम्या निर्दिष्टे पूर्वस्य कार्यं यथा स्यात्। अर्थे मा भूत्।”)
runs on from 6.2.64 (anuvṛtti)

a qualifier (viśeṣaṇa), agreeing with the word it qualifies (viśeṣya), stands for whatever ENDS in it — so we read “…-अन्त”; only the qualifier, never the qualified word (Nyāsa: “विशेषणेन चतदन्तविधिः [= च तदन्तविधिः], न विशेष्येण”)

A 7th-case word naming a following sound, suffix or word (“… परे”) puts the operation on what comes immediately before it. quote.q: Why do we say 'ending in मन् and अस्?' Observe सुराजन् and सुतक्षन् formed by the affix कनिन् (Unadi I.156), and the accent is on श and त, but with सु, the accent is thrown on the final by [[6.2.172]]. Why do we say with the exception of लोमन and उषत्? Observe सुलोम꣡न and सूष꣡स् [[6.2.172]].

paribhashas.effect: the word means its own form, not its meaning or synonyms

why.txt: runs on from 6.2.64 (anuvṛtti)
one vowel's accent is taught here, so the rest of the pada is anudātta — काशिका on 6.1.158: “यत्रान्यः स्वर उदात्तः स्वरितो वा विधीयते, तत्रानुदात्तं पदमेकं वर्जयित्वा भवतीत्येतदुपस्थितं द्रष्टव्यम्”
पुत्र here means the word पुत्र itself, not its meaning or its synonyms — काशिका on 1.1.68: “शास्त्रे स्वमेव रूपं शब्दस्य ग्राह्यं बोध्यं प्रत्याय्यं भवति, न बाह्योऽर्थः”

A 5th-case word of direction (‘after X’) puts the operation on what comes immediately after it — something already there (substitute, augment, elision, accent). Placing a new suffix is 3.1.2; a 5th of cause or ‘other than’, or an explicit पूर्व, is not this rule. (Kāśikā: “पञ्चम्यर्थनिर्देश उत्तरस्यैव कार्यं भवति”)
पुं here means the word पुं itself, not its meaning or its synonyms — काशिका on 1.1.68: “शास्त्रे स्वमेव रूपं शब्दस्य ग्राह्यं बोध्यं प्रत्याय्यं भवति, न बाह्योऽर्थः”

A 5th-case word of direction (‘after X’) puts the operation on what comes immediately after it — something already there (substitute, augment, elision, accent). Placing a new suffix is 3.1.2; a 5th of cause or ‘other than’, or an explicit पूर्व, is not this rule. (Kāśikā: “पञ्चम्यर्थनिर्देश उत्तरस्यैव कार्यं भवति”)

A suffix named as a known element stands for the word from the base it was added to up to that suffix (सन् → सन्नन्त). Not in saṃjñā rules or the uttarapada section, nor when the rule teaches or changes that suffix; as a 7th-case condition it means ‘what begins with it’. (Śekhara: “संज्ञाविधौ … तदन्तग्रहणं नास्ति”)

A 5th-case word of direction (‘after X’) puts the operation on what comes immediately after it — something already there (substitute, augment, elision, accent). Placing a new suffix is 3.1.2; a 5th of cause or ‘other than’, or an explicit पूर्व, is not this rule. (Kāśikā: “पञ्चम्यर्थनिर्देश उत्तरस्यैव कार्यं भवति”)

A suffix named as a known element stands for the word from the base it was added to up to that suffix (सन् → सन्नन्त). Not in saṃjñā rules or the uttarapada section, nor when the rule teaches or changes that suffix; as a 7th-case condition it means ‘what begins with it’. (Śekhara: “संज्ञाविधौ … तदन्तग्रहणं नास्ति”)

why.txt: A suffix named as a known element stands for the word from the base it was added to up to that suffix (सन् → सन्नन्त). why.txt: runs on from 6.2.155 (anuvṛtti)

A 5th-case word of direction (‘after X’) puts the operation on what comes immediately after it — something already there (substitute, augment, elision, accent). Placing a new suffix is 3.1.2; a 5th of cause or ‘other than’, or an explicit पूर्व, is not this rule. (Kāśikā: “पञ्चम्यर्थनिर्देश उत्तरस्यैव कार्यं भवति”)
runs on from 6.2.143 (anuvṛtti)

विभाषा names ‘not’ and ‘optionally’ together, so the rule's operation is optional; वा and अन्यतरस्याम् work the same way. A carried option word counts only where it is still in force (the commentary may call a rule nitya). बहुलम् is wider than an option. (Kāśikā: “विभाषाधिकारेऽपि नित्यसमास एवायम्।”)

why.txt: A suffix named as a known element stands for the word from the base it was added to up to that suffix (सन् → सन्नन्त). Not in saṃjñā rules or the uttarapada section, nor when the rule teaches or changes that suffix; as a 7th-case condition it means ‘what begins with it’. (Śekhara: “संज्ञाविधौ … तदन्तग्रहणं नास्ति”)
प्रथम here means the word प्रथम itself, not its meaning or its synonyms — काशिका on 1.1.68: “शास्त्रे स्वमेव रूपं शब्दस्य ग्राह्यं बोध्यं प्रत्याय्यं भवति, न बाह्योऽर्थः”

why.txt: runs on from 6.2.143 (anuvṛtti)

विभाषा names ‘not’ and ‘optionally’ together, so the rule's operation is optional; वा and अन्यतरस्याम् work the same way. A carried option word counts only where it is still in force (the commentary may call a rule nitya). बहुलम् is wider than an option. (Kāśikā: “विभाषाधिकारेऽपि नित्यसमास एवायम्।”)

why.txt: runs on from 6.3.1 (anuvṛtti)

Where a rule teaches a substitute, a 6th-case word whose link is otherwise unclear names what is replaced (“… स्थाने”). Not in augment rules (the 6th is the host), not where another word names the part replaced (उपधायाः, एचः), not where no substitute is taught. (Bhāṣya: “सन्देहे नियमः।”)

A 5th-case word of direction (‘after X’) puts the operation on what comes immediately after it — something already there (substitute, augment, elision, accent). Placing a new suffix is 3.1.2; a 5th of cause or ‘other than’, or an explicit पूर्व, is not this rule. (Kāśikā: “पञ्चम्यर्थनिर्देश उत्तरस्यैव कार्यं भवति”)
runs on from 6.3.1 (anuvṛtti)

A 7th-case word naming a following sound, suffix or word (“… परे”) puts the operation on what comes immediately before it. Not a 7th naming a meaning or domain (आर्धधातुके as ‘in its sphere’); if the rule also has a 5th, the 5th wins. (Bhāṣya: “शब्दे सप्तम्या निर्दिष्टे पूर्वस्य कार्यं यथा स्यात्। अर्थे मा भूत्।”)

why.txt: A 5th-case word of direction (‘after X’) puts the operation on what comes immediately after it — something already there (substitute, augment, elision, accent). Placing a new suffix is 3.1.2; a 5th of cause or ‘other than’, or an explicit पूर्व, is not this rule. (Kāśikā: “पञ्चम्यर्थनिर्देश उत्तरस्यैव कार्यं भवति”)

A 7th-case word naming a following sound, suffix or word (“… परे”) puts the operation on what comes immediately before it. Not a 7th naming a meaning or domain (आर्धधातुके as ‘in its sphere’); if the rule also has a 5th, the 5th wins. (Bhāṣya: “शब्दे सप्तम्या निर्दिष्टे पूर्वस्य कार्यं यथा स्यात्। अर्थे मा भूत्।”)
runs on from 6.3.1 (anuvṛtti)

विभाषा names ‘not’ and ‘optionally’ together, so the rule's operation is optional; वा and अन्यतरस्याम् work the same way. A carried option word counts only where it is still in force (the commentary may call a rule nitya). बहुलम् is wider than an option. (Kāśikā: “विभाषाधिकारेऽपि नित्यसमास एवायम्।”)

quote.q: As a general maxim, an affix denotes whenever it is employed in Grammar a word-form which begins with that to which that affix has been added, and ends with the affix itself (प्रत्ययग्रहणे यस्मात् स विहितस्तदादे स्तदन्तस्य ग्रहणम्)

why.txt: runs on from 6.3.9 (anuvṛtti)

A 5th-case word of direction (‘after X’) puts the operation on what comes immediately after it — something already there (substitute, augment, elision, accent). Placing a new suffix is 3.1.2; a 5th of cause or ‘other than’, or an explicit पूर्व, is not this rule. (Kāśikā: “पञ्चम्यर्थनिर्देश उत्तरस्यैव कार्यं भवति”)

why.txt: A 7th-case word naming a following sound, suffix or word (“… परे”) puts the operation on what comes immediately before it. why.txt: runs on from 6.3.16 (anuvṛtti)

विभाषा names ‘not’ and ‘optionally’ together, so the rule's operation is optional; वा and अन्यतरस्याम् work the same way. A carried option word counts only where it is still in force (the commentary may call a rule nitya). बहुलम् is wider than an option. (Kāśikā: “विभाषाधिकारेऽपि नित्यसमास एवायम्।”)

a qualifier (viśeṣaṇa), agreeing with the word it qualifies (viśeṣya), stands for whatever ENDS in it — so we read “…-अन्त”; only the qualifier, never the qualified word (Nyāsa: “विशेषणेन चतदन्तविधिः [= च तदन्तविधिः], न विशेष्येण”)

A 5th-case word of direction (‘after X’) puts the operation on what comes immediately after it — something already there (substitute, augment, elision, accent). Placing a new suffix is 3.1.2; a 5th of cause or ‘other than’, or an explicit पूर्व, is not this rule. (Kāśikā: “पञ्चम्यर्थनिर्देश उत्तरस्यैव कार्यं भवति”)

A 5th-case word of direction (‘after X’) puts the operation on what comes immediately after it — something already there (substitute, augment, elision, accent). Placing a new suffix is 3.1.2; a 5th of cause or ‘other than’, or an explicit पूर्व, is not this rule. (Kāśikā: “पञ्चम्यर्थनिर्देश उत्तरस्यैव कार्यं भवति”)

a qualifier (viśeṣaṇa), agreeing with the word it qualifies (viśeṣya), stands for whatever ENDS in it — so we read “…-अन्त”; only the qualifier, never the qualified word (Nyāsa: “विशेषणेन चतदन्तविधिः [= च तदन्तविधिः], न विशेष्येण”)

A 7th-case word naming a following sound, suffix or word (“… परे”) puts the operation on what comes immediately before it. Not a 7th naming a meaning or domain (आर्धधातुके as ‘in its sphere’); if the rule also has a 5th, the 5th wins. (Bhāṣya: “शब्दे सप्तम्या निर्दिष्टे पूर्वस्य कार्यं यथा स्यात्। अर्थे मा भूत्।”)
runs on from 6.3.1 (anuvṛtti)
runs on from 6.3.23 (anuvṛtti)

विभाषा names ‘not’ and ‘optionally’ together, so the rule's operation is optional; वा and अन्यतरस्याम् work the same way. A carried option word counts only where it is still in force (the commentary may call a rule nitya). बहुलम् is wider than an option. (Kāśikā: “विभाषाधिकारेऽपि नित्यसमास एवायम्।”)

why.txt: Where a rule teaches a substitute, a 6th-case word whose link is otherwise unclear names what is replaced (“… स्थाने”). Not in augment rules (the 6th is the host), not where another word names the part replaced (उपधायाः, एचः), not where no substitute is taught. (Bhāṣya: “सन्देहे नियमः।”)
runs on from 6.3.1 (anuvṛtti)

A 7th-case word naming a following sound, suffix or word (“… परे”) puts the operation on what comes immediately before it. Not a 7th naming a meaning or domain (आर्धधातुके as ‘in its sphere’); if the rule also has a 5th, the 5th wins. (Bhāṣya: “शब्दे सप्तम्या निर्दिष्टे पूर्वस्य कार्यं यथा स्यात्। अर्थे मा भूत्।”)

A 5th-case word of direction (‘after X’) puts the operation on what comes immediately after it — something already there (substitute, augment, elision, accent). Placing a new suffix is 3.1.2; a 5th of cause or ‘other than’, or an explicit पूर्व, is not this rule. (Kāśikā: “पञ्चम्यर्थनिर्देश उत्तरस्यैव कार्यं भवति”)

A 7th-case word naming a following sound, suffix or word (“… परे”) puts the operation on what comes immediately before it. Not a 7th naming a meaning or domain (आर्धधातुके as ‘in its sphere’); if the rule also has a 5th, the 5th wins. (Bhāṣya: “शब्दे सप्तम्या निर्दिष्टे पूर्वस्य कार्यं यथा स्यात्। अर्थे मा भूत्।”)

A suffix named as a known element stands for the word from the base it was added to up to that suffix (सन् → सन्नन्त). Not in saṃjñā rules or the uttarapada section, nor when the rule teaches or changes that suffix; as a 7th-case condition it means ‘what begins with it’. (Śekhara: “संज्ञाविधौ … तदन्तग्रहणं नास्ति”)

Where a rule teaches a substitute, a 6th-case word whose link is otherwise unclear names what is replaced (“… स्थाने”). Not in augment rules (the 6th is the host), not where another word names the part replaced (उपधायाः, एचः), not where no substitute is taught. (Bhāṣya: “सन्देहे नियमः।”)
a suffix named in a rule stands for the word that ENDS in that suffix (starting from what it was added to) — ङ्यन्तस्य — a pūrvapada ENDING in it
runs on from 6.3.34 (anuvṛtti)

A 5th-case word of direction (‘after X’) puts the operation on what comes immediately after it — something already there (substitute, augment, elision, accent). Placing a new suffix is 3.1.2; a 5th of cause or ‘other than’, or an explicit पूर्व, is not this rule. (Kāśikā: “पञ्चम्यर्थनिर्देश उत्तरस्यैव कार्यं भवति”)

A 7th-case word naming a following sound, suffix or word (“… परे”) puts the operation on what comes immediately before it. Not a 7th naming a meaning or domain (आर्धधातुके as ‘in its sphere’); if the rule also has a 5th, the 5th wins. (Bhāṣya: “शब्दे सप्तम्या निर्दिष्टे पूर्वस्य कार्यं यथा स्यात्। अर्थे मा भूत्।”)

why.txt: Where a rule teaches a substitute, a 6th-case word whose link is otherwise unclear names what is replaced (“… स्थाने”). Not in augment rules (the 6th is the host), not where another word names the part replaced (उपधायाः, एचः), not where no substitute is taught. (Bhāṣya: “सन्देहे नियमः।”)
द्व्यष्टन्त्रि here means the word द्व्यष्टन्त्रि itself, not its meaning or its synonyms — काशिका on 1.1.68: “शास्त्रे स्वमेव रूपं शब्दस्य ग्राह्यं बोध्यं प्रत्याय्यं भवति, न बाह्योऽर्थः”

runs on from 6.3.47 (anuvṛtti)

A 7th-case word naming a following sound, suffix or word (“… परे”) puts the operation on what comes immediately before it. Not a 7th naming a meaning or domain (आर्धधातुके as ‘in its sphere’); if the rule also has a 5th, the 5th wins. (Bhāṣya: “शब्दे सप्तम्या निर्दिष्टे पूर्वस्य कार्यं यथा स्यात्। अर्थे मा भूत्।”)
runs on from 6.3.47 (anuvṛtti)

विभाषा names ‘not’ and ‘optionally’ together, so the rule's operation is optional; वा and अन्यतरस्याम् work the same way. A carried option word counts only where it is still in force (the commentary may call a rule nitya). बहुलम् is wider than an option. (Kāśikā: “विभाषाधिकारेऽपि नित्यसमास एवायम्।”)
अबहुव्रीह्यशीत्योः (6.3.47) runs on as an exclusion: not in a bahuvrīhi, not before अशीति

why.txt: the augment stands in the 1st case
a टित् augment goes at the BEGINNING, a कित् one at the END — it goes at the BEGINNING of the place

A 5th-case word of direction (‘after X’) puts the operation on what comes immediately after it — something already there (substitute, augment, elision, accent). Placing a new suffix is 3.1.2; a 5th of cause or ‘other than’, or an explicit पूर्व, is not this rule. (Kāśikā: “पञ्चम्यर्थनिर्देश उत्तरस्यैव कार्यं भवति”)

Where a rule teaches a substitute, a 6th-case word whose link is otherwise unclear names what is replaced (“… स्थाने”). Not in augment rules (the 6th is the host), not where another word names the part replaced (उपधायाः, एचः), not where no substitute is taught. (Bhāṣya: “सन्देहे नियमः।”)
सह here means the word सह itself, not its meaning or its synonyms — काशिका on 1.1.68: “शास्त्रे स्वमेव रूपं शब्दस्य ग्राह्यं बोध्यं प्रत्याय्यं भवति, न बाह्योऽर्थः”

A 7th-case word naming a following sound, suffix or word (“… परे”) puts the operation on what comes immediately before it. Not a 7th naming a meaning or domain (आर्धधातुके as ‘in its sphere’); if the rule also has a 5th, the 5th wins. (Bhāṣya: “शब्दे सप्तम्या निर्दिष्टे पूर्वस्य कार्यं यथा स्यात्। अर्थे मा भूत्।”)

why.txt: runs on from 6.3.78 (anuvṛtti)

Where a rule teaches a substitute, a 6th-case word whose link is otherwise unclear names what is replaced (“… स्थाने”). Not in augment rules (the 6th is the host), not where another word names the part replaced (उपधायाः, एचः), not where no substitute is taught. (Bhāṣya: “सन्देहे नियमः।”)

A 7th-case word naming a following sound, suffix or word (“… परे”) puts the operation on what comes immediately before it. Not a 7th naming a meaning or domain (आर्धधातुके as ‘in its sphere’); if the rule also has a 5th, the 5th wins. (Bhāṣya: “शब्दे सप्तम्या निर्दिष्टे पूर्वस्य कार्यं यथा स्यात्। अर्थे मा भूत्।”)

a word in the 6th case in a rule names WHAT IS REPLACED — so we read “… स्थाने” — names the place — the thing replaced (“स्थाने”)

A 7th-case word naming a following sound, suffix or word (“… परे”) puts the operation on what comes immediately before it. Not a 7th naming a meaning or domain (आर्धधातुके as ‘in its sphere’); if the rule also has a 5th, the 5th wins. (Bhāṣya: “शब्दे सप्तम्या निर्दिष्टे पूर्वस्य कार्यं यथा स्यात्। अर्थे मा भूत्।”)

a SOUND (a letter, a pratyāhāra, or the augment इट् — not a suffix or a word) in the 7th case, qualifying a 7th-case condition, stands for what BEGINS with it — so we read “…-आदि” (an exception to tadanta-vidhi, 1.1.72) — → यकारादौ (what BEGINS with it)

विभाषा names ‘not’ and ‘optionally’ together, so the rule's operation is optional; वा and अन्यतरस्याम् work the same way. By [[1.1.54]], ई replaces the first-letter of अप् viz अ only. Thus द्वीपः, अन्तरीपः, नीपम्, वीपम्, समीपम्

paribhashas.trigger: ईत्: ई with त् after it (तपर)
paribhashas.effect: only the long ई, not its other lengths
the ई replaces the first sound of अप् after द्वि/अन्तर्/an upasarga (BM)

why.txt: A vowel with त् after it stands only for vowels of its own length: अत् = short अ, आत् = long आ, एत्/ओत् = two-mora ए/ओ, not pluta. Check it is a real tapara: आत् may be the 5th case of अ (आद्गुणः), and a त् may belong to the form. (Kāśikā: “तपरो वर्णस्तत्कालस्यात्मना तुल्यकालस्य … ग्राहको भवति”)

the ई replaces the first sound of अप् after द्वि/अन्तर्/an upasarga — BM

A 5th-case word of direction (‘after X’) puts the operation on what comes immediately after it — something already there (substitute, augment, elision, accent). why.txt: runs on from 6.3.1 (anuvṛtti)
runs on from 6.3.104 (anuvṛtti)
a substitute of more than one sound (or शित्) replaces the WHOLE — it replaces the WHOLE of the place
runs on from 6.3.101 (anuvṛtti)

Where a rule teaches a substitute, a 6th-case word whose link is otherwise unclear names what is replaced (“… स्थाने”). Not in augment rules (the 6th is the host), not where another word names the part replaced (उपधायाः, एचः), not where no substitute is taught. (Bhāṣya: “सन्देहे नियमः।”)

A 7th-case word naming a following sound, suffix or word (“… परे”) puts the operation on what comes immediately before it. Not a 7th naming a meaning or domain (आर्धधातुके as ‘in its sphere’); if the rule also has a 5th, the 5th wins. (Bhāṣya: “शब्दे सप्तम्या निर्दिष्टे पूर्वस्य कार्यं यथा स्यात्। अर्थे मा भूत्।”)
पुरुष here means the word पुरुष itself, not its meaning or its synonyms — काशिका on 1.1.68: “शास्त्रे स्वमेव रूपं शब्दस्य ग्राह्यं बोध्यं प्रत्याय्यं भवति, न बाह्योऽर्थः”

विभाषा names ‘not’ and ‘optionally’ together, so the rule's operation is optional; वा and अन्यतरस्याम् work the same way. A carried option word counts only where it is still in force (the commentary may call a rule nitya). बहुलम् is wider than an option. (Kāśikā: “विभाषाधिकारेऽपि नित्यसमास एवायम्।”)

Where a rule teaches a substitute, a 6th-case word whose link is otherwise unclear names what is replaced (“… स्थाने”). Not in augment rules (the 6th is the host), not where another word names the part replaced (उपधायाः, एचः), not where no substitute is taught. (Bhāṣya: “सन्देहे नियमः।”)

A 7th-case word naming a following sound, suffix or word (“… परे”) puts the operation on what comes immediately before it. Not a 7th naming a meaning or domain (आर्धधातुके as ‘in its sphere’); if the rule also has a 5th, the 5th wins. (Bhāṣya: “शब्दे सप्तम्या निर्दिष्टे पूर्वस्य कार्यं यथा स्यात्। अर्थे मा भूत्।”)

why.txt: runs on from 6.3.111 (anuvṛtti)
दीर्घ is taught by its own name, so it falls only on a vowel (अचः) — काशिका on 1.2.28: “ह्रस्वदीर्घप्लुताः स्वसंज्ञया शिष्यमाणा अच एव स्थाने वेदितव्याः”

Where a rule teaches a substitute, a 6th-case word whose link is otherwise unclear names what is replaced (“… स्थाने”). Not in augment rules (the 6th is the host), not where another word names the part replaced (उपधायाः, एचः), not where no substitute is taught. (Bhāṣya: “सन्देहे नियमः।”)

A 7th-case word naming a following sound, suffix or word (“… परे”) puts the operation on what comes immediately before it. Not a 7th naming a meaning or domain (आर्धधातुके as ‘in its sphere’); if the rule also has a 5th, the 5th wins. (Bhāṣya: “शब्दे सप्तम्या निर्दिष्टे पूर्वस्य कार्यं यथा स्यात्। अर्थे मा भूत्।”)

A 7th-case word naming a following sound, suffix or word (“… परे”) puts the operation on what comes immediately before it. Not a 7th naming a meaning or domain (आर्धधातुके as ‘in its sphere’); if the rule also has a 5th, the 5th wins. (Bhāṣya: “शब्दे सप्तम्या निर्दिष्टे पूर्वस्य कार्यं यथा स्यात्। अर्थे मा भूत्।”)

a qualifier (viśeṣaṇa), agreeing with the word it qualifies (viśeṣya), stands for whatever ENDS in it — so we read “…-अन्त”; only the qualifier, never the qualified word (Nyāsa: “विशेषणेन चतदन्तविधिः [= च तदन्तविधिः], न विशेष्येण”)

Where a rule teaches a substitute, a 6th-case word whose link is otherwise unclear names what is replaced (“… स्थाने”). Not in augment rules (the 6th is the host), not where another word names the part replaced (उपधायाः, एचः), not where no substitute is taught. (Bhāṣya: “सन्देहे नियमः।”)

A 7th-case word naming a following sound, suffix or word (“… परे”) puts the operation on what comes immediately before it. Not a 7th naming a meaning or domain (आर्धधातुके as ‘in its sphere’); if the rule also has a 5th, the 5th wins. (Bhāṣya: “शब्दे सप्तम्या निर्दिष्टे पूर्वस्य कार्यं यथा स्यात्। अर्थे मा भूत्।”)

What a suffix was introduced after — a dhātu or prātipadika, with any vikaraṇa or augment added to it — is the aṅga of that suffix. The अङ्गस्य heading (6.4.1) runs to the end of book 7; it names the base, not necessarily the part that changes. (Kāśikā: “यस्मात् प्रत्ययो विधीयते … प्रत्यये परतोऽङ्गसंज्ञं भवति।”)

A 7th-case word naming a following sound, suffix or word (“… परे”) puts the operation on what comes immediately before it. Not a 7th naming a meaning or domain (आर्धधातुके as ‘in its sphere’); if the rule also has a 5th, the 5th wins. (Bhāṣya: “शब्दे सप्तम्या निर्दिष्टे पूर्वस्य कार्यं यथा स्यात्। अर्थे मा भूत्।”)

why.txt: runs on from 6.4.1 (anuvṛtti)

What a suffix was introduced after — a dhātu or prātipadika, with any vikaraṇa or augment added to it — is the aṅga of that suffix. The अङ्गस्य heading (6.4.1) runs to the end of book 7; it names the base, not necessarily the part that changes. (Kāśikā: “यस्मात् प्रत्ययो विधीयते … प्रत्यये परतोऽङ्गसंज्ञं भवति।”)

why.txt: A suffix named as a known element stands for the word from the base it was added to up to that suffix (सन् → सन्नन्त). Not in saṃjñā rules or the uttarapada section, nor when the rule teaches or changes that suffix; as a 7th-case condition it means ‘what begins with it’. (Śekhara: “संज्ञाविधौ … तदन्तग्रहणं नास्ति”)

no.txt: not the place (a prakriti)

why.txt: runs on from 6.4.8 (anuvṛtti)

A 7th-case word naming a following sound, suffix or word (“… परे”) puts the operation on what comes immediately before it. Not a 7th naming a meaning or domain (आर्धधातुके as ‘in its sphere’); if the rule also has a 5th, the 5th wins. (Bhāṣya: “शब्दे सप्तम्या निर्दिष्टे पूर्वस्य कार्यं यथा स्यात्। अर्थे मा भूत्।”)
runs on from 6.4.8 (anuvṛtti)

What a suffix was introduced after — a dhātu or prātipadika, with any vikaraṇa or augment added to it — is the aṅga of that suffix. The अङ्गस्य heading (6.4.1) runs to the end of book 7; it names the base, not necessarily the part that changes. (Kāśikā: “यस्मात् प्रत्ययो विधीयते … प्रत्यये परतोऽङ्गसंज्ञं भवति।”)

Where a rule teaches a substitute, a 6th-case word whose link is otherwise unclear names what is replaced (“… स्थाने”). Not in augment rules (the 6th is the host), not where another word names the part replaced (उपधायाः, एचः), not where no substitute is taught. (Bhāṣya: “सन्देहे नियमः।”)

why.txt: runs on from 6.4.1 (anuvṛtti)

What a suffix was introduced after — a dhātu or prātipadika, with any vikaraṇa or augment added to it — is the aṅga of that suffix. The अङ्गस्य heading (6.4.1) runs to the end of book 7; it names the base, not necessarily the part that changes. (Kāśikā: “यस्मात् प्रत्ययो विधीयते … प्रत्यये परतोऽङ्गसंज्ञं भवति।”)
as the प्रथमावृत्तिः reads it

A 5th-case word of direction (‘after X’) puts the operation on what comes immediately after it — something already there (substitute, augment, elision, accent). Placing a new suffix is 3.1.2; a 5th of cause or ‘other than’, or an explicit पूर्व, is not this rule. (Kāśikā: “पञ्चम्यर्थनिर्देश उत्तरस्यैव कार्यं भवति”)
a suffix named in a rule stands for the word that ENDS in that suffix (starting from what it was added to) — श्नमन्तात् अङ्गात् — an aṅga ENDING in it

A 7th-case word naming a following sound, suffix or word (“… परे”) puts the operation on what comes immediately before it. Not a 7th naming a meaning or domain (आर्धधातुके as ‘in its sphere’); if the rule also has a 5th, the 5th wins. (Bhāṣya: “शब्दे सप्तम्या निर्दिष्टे पूर्वस्य कार्यं यथा स्यात्। अर्थे मा भूत्।”)

विभाषा names ‘not’ and ‘optionally’ together, so the rule's operation is optional; वा and अन्यतरस्याम् work the same way. A carried option word counts only where it is still in force (the commentary may call a rule nitya). बहुलम् is wider than an option. (Kāśikā: “विभाषाधिकारेऽपि नित्यसमास एवायम्।”)

Where a rule teaches a substitute, a 6th-case word whose link is otherwise unclear names what is replaced (“… स्थाने”). Not in augment rules (the 6th is the host), not where another word names the part replaced (उपधायाः, एचः), not where no substitute is taught. (Bhāṣya: “सन्देहे नियमः।”)

What a suffix was introduced after — a dhātu or prātipadika, with any vikaraṇa or augment added to it — is the aṅga of that suffix. The अङ्गस्य heading (6.4.1) runs to the end of book 7; it names the base, not necessarily the part that changes. (Kāśikā: “यस्मात् प्रत्ययो विधीयते … प्रत्यये परतोऽङ्गसंज्ञं भवति।”)

A 7th-case word naming a following sound, suffix or word (“… परे”) puts the operation on what comes immediately before it. Not a 7th naming a meaning or domain (आर्धधातुके as ‘in its sphere’); if the rule also has a 5th, the 5th wins. (Bhāṣya: “शब्दे सप्तम्या निर्दिष्टे पूर्वस्य कार्यं यथा स्यात्। अर्थे मा भूत्।”)

What a suffix was introduced after — a dhātu or prātipadika, with any vikaraṇa or augment added to it — is the aṅga of that suffix. The अङ्गस्य heading (6.4.1) runs to the end of book 7; it names the base, not necessarily the part that changes. (Kāśikā: “यस्मात् प्रत्ययो विधीयते … प्रत्यये परतोऽङ्गसंज्ञं भवति।”)

A 7th-case word naming a following sound, suffix or word (“… परे”) puts the operation on what comes immediately before it. Not a 7th naming a meaning or domain (आर्धधातुके as ‘in its sphere’); if the rule also has a 5th, the 5th wins. (Bhāṣya: “शब्दे सप्तम्या निर्दिष्टे पूर्वस्य कार्यं यथा स्यात्। अर्थे मा भूत्।”)

why.txt: runs on from 6.4.41 (anuvṛtti)

Where a rule teaches a substitute, a 6th-case word whose link is otherwise unclear names what is replaced (“… स्थाने”). Not in augment rules (the 6th is the host), not where another word names the part replaced (उपधायाः, एचः), not where no substitute is taught. (Bhāṣya: “सन्देहे नियमः।”)

What a suffix was introduced after — a dhātu or prātipadika, with any vikaraṇa or augment added to it — is the aṅga of that suffix. The अङ्गस्य heading (6.4.1) runs to the end of book 7; it names the base, not necessarily the part that changes. (Kāśikā: “यस्मात् प्रत्ययो विधीयते … प्रत्यये परतोऽङ्गसंज्ञं भवति।”)
तनोतेः: dhātu named in its श्तिप् form → = the dhātu तन्

A 7th-case word naming a following sound, suffix or word (“… परे”) puts the operation on what comes immediately before it. Not a 7th naming a meaning or domain (आर्धधातुके as ‘in its sphere’); if the rule also has a 5th, the 5th wins. (Bhāṣya: “शब्दे सप्तम्या निर्दिष्टे पूर्वस्य कार्यं यथा स्यात्। अर्थे मा भूत्।”)

q: on which stem (aṅga) does it operate?

why.txt: runs on from 6.4.1 (anuvṛtti)

What a suffix was introduced after — a dhātu or prātipadika, with any vikaraṇa or augment added to it — is the aṅga of that suffix. The अङ्गस्य heading (6.4.1) runs to the end of book 7; it names the base, not necessarily the part that changes. (Kāśikā: “यस्मात् प्रत्ययो विधीयते … प्रत्यये परतोऽङ्गसंज्ञं भवति।”)
the elision takes the first sound of क्य after the consonant — SK

Where a rule teaches a substitute, a 6th-case word whose link is otherwise unclear names what is replaced (“… स्थाने”). Not in augment rules (the 6th is the host), not where another word names the part replaced (उपधायाः, एचः), not where no substitute is taught. (Bhāṣya: “सन्देहे नियमः।”)
runs on from 6.4.49 (anuvṛtti)

A 5th-case word of direction (‘after X’) puts the operation on what comes immediately after it — something already there (substitute, augment, elision, accent). Placing a new suffix is 3.1.2; a 5th of cause or ‘other than’, or an explicit पूर्व, is not this rule. (Kāśikā: “पञ्चम्यर्थनिर्देश उत्तरस्यैव कार्यं भवति”)
runs on from 6.4.46 (anuvṛtti)
a word in the 7th case names what must FOLLOW — so we read “… परे” — names what FOLLOWS — the operation is on what precedes it

विभाषा names ‘not’ and ‘optionally’ together, so the rule's operation is optional; वा and अन्यतरस्याम् work the same way. A carried option word counts only where it is still in force (the commentary may call a rule nitya). बहुलम् is wider than an option. (Kāśikā: “विभाषाधिकारेऽपि नित्यसमास एवायम्।”)

The अङ्गस्य heading (6.4.1) runs to the end of book 7; it names the base, not necessarily the part that changes. (Kāśikā: “यस्मात् प्रत्ययो विधीयते … प्रत्यये परतोऽङ्गसंज्ञं भवति।”)
runs on from 6.4.51 (anuvṛtti)

Where a rule teaches a substitute, a 6th-case word whose link is otherwise unclear names what is replaced (“… स्थाने”). Not in augment rules (the 6th is the host), not where another word names the part replaced (उपधायाः, एचः), not where no substitute is taught. (Bhāṣya: “सन्देहे नियमः।”)

A 5th-case word of direction (‘after X’) puts the operation on what comes immediately after it — something already there (substitute, augment, elision, accent). Placing a new suffix is 3.1.2; a 5th of cause or ‘other than’, or an explicit पूर्व, is not this rule. (Kāśikā: “पञ्चम्यर्थनिर्देश उत्तरस्यैव कार्यं भवति”)

A 7th-case word naming a following sound, suffix or word (“… परे”) puts the operation on what comes immediately before it. Not a 7th naming a meaning or domain (आर्धधातुके as ‘in its sphere’); if the rule also has a 5th, the 5th wins. (Bhāṣya: “शब्दे सप्तम्या निर्दिष्टे पूर्वस्य कार्यं यथा स्यात्। अर्थे मा भूत्।”)

Where a rule teaches a substitute, a 6th-case word whose link is otherwise unclear names what is replaced (“… स्थाने”). Not in augment rules (the 6th is the host), not where another word names the part replaced (उपधायाः, एचः), not where no substitute is taught. (Bhāṣya: “सन्देहे नियमः।”)

What a suffix was introduced after — a dhātu or prātipadika, with any vikaraṇa or augment added to it — is the aṅga of that suffix. The अङ्गस्य heading (6.4.1) runs to the end of book 7; it names the base, not necessarily the part that changes. (Kāśikā: “यस्मात् प्रत्ययो विधीयते … प्रत्यये परतोऽङ्गसंज्ञं भवति।”)

What a suffix was introduced after — a dhātu or prātipadika, with any vikaraṇa or augment added to it — is the aṅga of that suffix. The अङ्गस्य heading (6.4.1) runs to the end of book 7; it names the base, not necessarily the part that changes. (Kāśikā: “यस्मात् प्रत्ययो विधीयते … प्रत्यये परतोऽङ्गसंज्ञं भवति।”)

A 5th-case word of direction (‘after X’) puts the operation on what comes immediately after it — something already there (substitute, augment, elision, accent). Placing a new suffix is 3.1.2; a 5th of cause or ‘other than’, or an explicit पूर्व, is not this rule. (Kāśikā: “पञ्चम्यर्थनिर्देश उत्तरस्यैव कार्यं भवति”)

why.txt: runs on from 6.4.1 (anuvṛtti)

What a suffix was introduced after — a dhātu or prātipadika, with any vikaraṇa or augment added to it — is the aṅga of that suffix. The अङ्गस्य heading (6.4.1) runs to the end of book 7; it names the base, not necessarily the part that changes. (Kāśikā: “यस्मात् प्रत्ययो विधीयते … प्रत्यये परतोऽङ्गसंज्ञं भवति।”)
the substitute stands in the 1st case — Mahābhāṣya on 1.1.57: “आदेशः प्रथमानिर्दिष्टः”
लोपः → non-appearance; it counts as a replacement
आतः qualifies अङ्गस्य (the heading from 6.4.1, both in the 6th) — a qualifier agreeing with the word it qualifies stands for whatever ends in it → “आकारान्तस्य स्थाने”

Where a rule teaches a substitute, a 6th-case word whose link is otherwise unclear names what is replaced (“… स्थाने”). Not in augment rules (the 6th is the host), not where another word names the part replaced (उपधायाः, एचः), not where no substitute is taught. (Bhāṣya: “सन्देहे नियमः।”)

A 7th-case word naming a following sound, suffix or word (“… परे”) puts the operation on what comes immediately before it. q: on which stem (aṅga) does it operate?

why.txt: runs on from 6.4.1 (anuvṛtti)

What a suffix was introduced after — a dhātu or prātipadika, with any vikaraṇa or augment added to it — is the aṅga of that suffix. The अङ्गस्य heading (6.4.1) runs to the end of book 7; it names the base, not necessarily the part that changes. (Kāśikā: “यस्मात् प्रत्ययो विधीयते … प्रत्यये परतोऽङ्गसंज्ञं भवति।”)

Where a rule teaches a substitute, a 6th-case word whose link is otherwise unclear names what is replaced (“… स्थाने”). Not in augment rules (the 6th is the host), not where another word names the part replaced (उपधायाः, एचः), not where no substitute is taught. (Bhāṣya: “सन्देहे नियमः।”)

Where a rule allows several substitutes for one original (guṇa = अ/ए/ओ; a class like जश्), the one most like it is chosen — by place of articulation first, then effort, length or meaning (चेता, स्तोता). Where a rule teaches a substitute, a 6th-case word whose link is otherwise unclear names what is replaced (“… स्थाने”). Not in augment rules (the 6th is the host), not where another word names the part replaced (उपधायाः, एचः), not where no substitute is taught. (Bhāṣya: “सन्देहे नियमः।”)

A 7th-case word naming a following sound, suffix or word (“… परे”) puts the operation on what comes immediately before it. Not a 7th naming a meaning or domain (आर्धधातुके as ‘in its sphere’); if the rule also has a 5th, the 5th wins. (Bhāṣya: “शब्दे सप्तम्या निर्दिष्टे पूर्वस्य कार्यं यथा स्यात्। अर्थे मा भूत्।”)
runs on from 6.4.1 (anuvṛtti)

why.txt: runs on from 6.4.81 (anuvṛtti)

When one sound is taught in place of a longer item named in the 6th case, it replaces only that item's last sound. Not when the place is itself one sound or a position (उपधा, टि), not for augments, and not for लुक् — the whole suffix goes. (Nyāsa: “आदेशः पुनरत्रैकाल्लभ्यते।”)

A suffix named as a known element stands for the word from the base it was added to up to that suffix (सन् → सन्नन्त). Not in saṃjñā rules or the uttarapada section, nor when the rule teaches or changes that suffix; as a 7th-case condition it means ‘what begins with it’. (Śekhara: “संज्ञाविधौ … तदन्तग्रहणं नास्ति”)

Where a rule teaches a substitute, a 6th-case word whose link is otherwise unclear names what is replaced (“… स्थाने”). Not in augment rules (the 6th is the host), not where another word names the part replaced (उपधायाः, एचः), not where no substitute is taught. (Bhāṣya: “सन्देहे नियमः।”)

A suffix named as a known element stands for the word from the base it was added to up to that suffix (सन् → सन्नन्त). Not in saṃjñā rules or the uttarapada section, nor when the rule teaches or changes that suffix; as a 7th-case condition it means ‘what begins with it’. (Śekhara: “संज्ञाविधौ … तदन्तग्रहणं नास्ति”)

A 7th-case word naming a following sound, suffix or word (“… परे”) puts the operation on what comes immediately before it. Not a 7th naming a meaning or domain (आर्धधातुके as ‘in its sphere’); if the rule also has a 5th, the 5th wins. (Bhāṣya: “शब्दे सप्तम्या निर्दिष्टे पूर्वस्य कार्यं यथा स्यात्। अर्थे मा भूत्।”)

An augment (āgama) marked ṭ is joined as the first part, one marked k as the last part, of the item named in the 6th case; with a 5th case it goes on what follows. It replaces nothing, and a ṭ/k marker on a suffix or a substitute does not bring in this rule. (Kāśikā: “आदिष्टिद् भवति अन्तःकिद् भवति षष्ठीनिर्दिष्टस्य”)

why.txt: A vowel with त् after it stands only for vowels of its own length: अत् = short अ, आत् = long आ, एत्/ओत् = two-mora ए/ओ, not pluta. q: on which stem (aṅga) does it operate?

why.txt: runs on from 6.4.1 (anuvṛtti)

What a suffix was introduced after — a dhātu or prātipadika, with any vikaraṇa or augment added to it — is the aṅga of that suffix. The अङ्गस्य heading (6.4.1) runs to the end of book 7; it names the base, not necessarily the part that changes. (Kāśikā: “यस्मात् प्रत्ययो विधीयते … प्रत्यये परतोऽङ्गसंज्ञं भवति।”)

Where a rule teaches a substitute, a 6th-case word whose link is otherwise unclear names what is replaced (“… स्थाने”). Not in augment rules (the 6th is the host), not where another word names the part replaced (उपधायाः, एचः), not where no substitute is taught. (Bhāṣya: “सन्देहे नियमः।”)

A 5th-case word of direction (‘after X’) puts the operation on what comes immediately after it — something already there (substitute, augment, elision, accent). Placing a new suffix is 3.1.2; a 5th of cause or ‘other than’, or an explicit पूर्व, is not this rule. (Kāśikā: “पञ्चम्यर्थनिर्देश उत्तरस्यैव कार्यं भवति”)

a qualifier (viśeṣaṇa), agreeing with the word it qualifies (viśeṣya), stands for whatever ENDS in it — so we read “…-अन्त”; only the qualifier, never the qualified word (Nyāsa: “विशेषणेन चतदन्तविधिः [= च तदन्तविधिः], न विशेष्येण”) — हु झलन्तेभ्यः — what ENDS in it, as the नैलेश-वृत्तिः, prathamāvṛtti and Kāśikā read it

why.txt: runs on from 6.4.104 (anuvṛtti)

Where a rule teaches a substitute, a 6th-case word whose link is otherwise unclear names what is replaced (“… स्थाने”). Not in augment rules (the 6th is the host), not where another word names the part replaced (उपधायाः, एचः), not where no substitute is taught. (Bhāṣya: “सन्देहे नियमः।”)

a qualifier (viśeṣaṇa), agreeing with the word it qualifies (viśeṣya), stands for whatever ENDS in it — so we read “…-अन्त”; only the qualifier, never the qualified word (Nyāsa: “विशेषणेन चतदन्तविधिः [= च तदन्तविधिः], न विशेष्येण”)

A 5th-case word of direction (‘after X’) puts the operation on what comes immediately after it — something already there (substitute, augment, elision, accent). Placing a new suffix is 3.1.2; a 5th of cause or ‘other than’, or an explicit पूर्व, is not this rule. (Kāśikā: “पञ्चम्यर्थनिर्देश उत्तरस्यैव कार्यं भवति”)
runs on from 6.4.1 (anuvṛtti)

What a suffix was introduced after — a dhātu or prātipadika, with any vikaraṇa or augment added to it — is the aṅga of that suffix. The अङ्गस्य heading (6.4.1) runs to the end of book 7; it names the base, not necessarily the part that changes. (Kāśikā: “यस्मात् प्रत्ययो विधीयते … प्रत्यये परतोऽङ्गसंज्ञं भवति।”)

why.txt: runs on from 6.4.1 (anuvṛtti)

What a suffix was introduced after — a dhātu or prātipadika, with any vikaraṇa or augment added to it — is the aṅga of that suffix. The अङ्गस्य heading (6.4.1) runs to the end of book 7; it names the base, not necessarily the part that changes. (Kāśikā: “यस्मात् प्रत्ययो विधीयते … प्रत्यये परतोऽङ्गसंज्ञं भवति।”)

Where a rule teaches a substitute, a 6th-case word whose link is otherwise unclear names what is replaced (“… स्थाने”). Not in augment rules (the 6th is the host), not where another word names the part replaced (उपधायाः, एचः), not where no substitute is taught. (Bhāṣya: “सन्देहे नियमः।”)

a SOUND (a letter, a pratyāhāra, or the augment इट् — not a suffix or a word) in the 7th case, qualifying a 7th-case condition, stands for what BEGINS with it — so we read “…-आदि” (an exception to tadanta-vidhi, 1.1.72)

A 7th-case word naming a following sound, suffix or word (“… परे”) puts the operation on what comes immediately before it. Not a 7th naming a meaning or domain (आर्धधातुके as ‘in its sphere’); if the rule also has a 5th, the 5th wins. (Bhāṣya: “शब्दे सप्तम्या निर्दिष्टे पूर्वस्य कार्यं यथा स्यात्। अर्थे मा भूत्।”)

What a suffix was introduced after — a dhātu or prātipadika, with any vikaraṇa or augment added to it — is the aṅga of that suffix. The अङ्गस्य heading (6.4.1) runs to the end of book 7; it names the base, not necessarily the part that changes. (Kāśikā: “यस्मात् प्रत्ययो विधीयते … प्रत्यये परतोऽङ्गसंज्ञं भवति।”)
runs on from 6.4.106 (anuvṛtti)
a vowel with त् after it (तपर) means only that one length — only the short उ
उतः (carried over from 6.4.106) qualifies अङ्गस्य (the heading from 6.4.1) — a qualifier agreeing with the word it qualifies stands for whatever ends in it → “उकारस्य”
runs on from 6.4.108 (anuvṛtti)

A 5th-case word of direction (‘after X’) puts the operation on what comes immediately after it — something already there (substitute, augment, elision, accent). Placing a new suffix is 3.1.2; a 5th of cause or ‘other than’, or an explicit पूर्व, is not this rule. (Kāśikā: “पञ्चम्यर्थनिर्देश उत्तरस्यैव कार्यं भवति”)
करोतेः: dhātu named in its श्तिप् form → = the dhātu कृ

A 7th-case word naming a following sound, suffix or word (“… परे”) puts the operation on what comes immediately before it. Not a 7th naming a meaning or domain (आर्धधातुके as ‘in its sphere’); if the rule also has a 5th, the 5th wins. (Bhāṣya: “शब्दे सप्तम्या निर्दिष्टे पूर्वस्य कार्यं यथा स्यात्। अर्थे मा भूत्।”)

a SOUND (a letter, a pratyāhāra, or the augment इट् — not a suffix or a word) in the 7th case, qualifying a 7th-case condition, stands for what BEGINS with it — so we read “…-आदि” (an exception to tadanta-vidhi, 1.1.72)

why.txt: runs on from 6.4.1 (anuvṛtti)

What a suffix was introduced after — a dhātu or prātipadika, with any vikaraṇa or augment added to it — is the aṅga of that suffix. The अङ्गस्य heading (6.4.1) runs to the end of book 7; it names the base, not necessarily the part that changes. (Kāśikā: “यस्मात् प्रत्ययो विधीयते … प्रत्यये परतोऽङ्गसंज्ञं भवति।”)

Where a rule teaches a substitute, a 6th-case word whose link is otherwise unclear names what is replaced (“… स्थाने”). Not in augment rules (the 6th is the host), not where another word names the part replaced (उपधायाः, एचः), not where no substitute is taught. (Bhāṣya: “सन्देहे नियमः।”)

paribhashas.trigger: इत्: इ with त् after it (तपर)
paribhashas.effect: only the short इ, not its other lengths

why.txt: A vowel with त् after it stands only for vowels of its own length: अत् = short अ, आत् = long आ, एत्/ओत् = two-mora ए/ओ, not pluta. Check it is a real tapara: आत् may be the 5th case of अ (आद्गुणः), and a त् may belong to the form. (Kāśikā: “तपरो वर्णस्तत्कालस्यात्मना तुल्यकालस्य … ग्राहको भवति”)

q: on which stem (aṅga) does it operate?

why.txt: runs on from 6.4.1 (anuvṛtti)

What a suffix was introduced after — a dhātu or prātipadika, with any vikaraṇa or augment added to it — is the aṅga of that suffix. The अङ्गस्य heading (6.4.1) runs to the end of book 7; it names the base, not necessarily the part that changes. (Kāśikā: “यस्मात् प्रत्ययो विधीयते … प्रत्यये परतोऽङ्गसंज्ञं भवति।”)
runs on from 6.4.112 (anuvṛtti)

Where a rule teaches a substitute, a 6th-case word whose link is otherwise unclear names what is replaced (“… स्थाने”). Not in augment rules (the 6th is the host), not where another word names the part replaced (उपधायाः, एचः), not where no substitute is taught. (Bhāṣya: “सन्देहे नियमः।”)
runs on from 6.4.110 (anuvṛtti)

A 7th-case word naming a following sound, suffix or word (“… परे”) puts the operation on what comes immediately before it. Not a 7th naming a meaning or domain (आर्धधातुके as ‘in its sphere’); if the rule also has a 5th, the 5th wins. (Bhāṣya: “शब्दे सप्तम्या निर्दिष्टे पूर्वस्य कार्यं यथा स्यात्। अर्थे मा भूत्।”)
runs on from 6.4.98 (anuvṛtti)
runs on from 6.4.113 (anuvṛtti)

a SOUND (a letter, a pratyāhāra, or the augment इट् — not a suffix or a word) in the 7th case, qualifying a 7th-case condition, stands for what BEGINS with it — so we read “…-आदि” (an exception to tadanta-vidhi, 1.1.72)

Where a rule teaches a substitute, a 6th-case word whose link is otherwise unclear names what is replaced (“… स्थाने”). Not in augment rules (the 6th is the host), not where another word names the part replaced (उपधायाः, एचः), not where no substitute is taught. (Bhāṣya: “सन्देहे नियमः।”)

why.txt: runs on from 6.4.1 (anuvṛtti)

What a suffix was introduced after — a dhātu or prātipadika, with any vikaraṇa or augment added to it — is the aṅga of that suffix. The अङ्गस्य heading (6.4.1) runs to the end of book 7; it names the base, not necessarily the part that changes. (Kāśikā: “यस्मात् प्रत्ययो विधीयते … प्रत्यये परतोऽङ्गसंज्ञं भवति।”)

Where a rule teaches a substitute, a 6th-case word whose link is otherwise unclear names what is replaced (“… स्थाने”). Not in augment rules (the 6th is the host), not where another word names the part replaced (उपधायाः, एचः), not where no substitute is taught. (Bhāṣya: “सन्देहे नियमः।”)

A 7th-case word naming a following sound, suffix or word (“… परे”) puts the operation on what comes immediately before it. Not a 7th naming a meaning or domain (आर्धधातुके as ‘in its sphere’); if the rule also has a 5th, the 5th wins. (Bhāṣya: “शब्दे सप्तम्या निर्दिष्टे पूर्वस्य कार्यं यथा स्यात्। अर्थे मा भूत्।”)

q: on which stem (aṅga) does it operate?

why.txt: runs on from 6.4.1 (anuvṛtti)

What a suffix was introduced after — a dhātu or prātipadika, with any vikaraṇa or augment added to it — is the aṅga of that suffix. The अङ्गस्य heading (6.4.1) runs to the end of book 7; it names the base, not necessarily the part that changes. (Kāśikā: “यस्मात् प्रत्ययो विधीयते … प्रत्यये परतोऽङ्गसंज्ञं भवति।”)
runs on from 6.4.120 (anuvṛtti)

Where a rule teaches a substitute, a 6th-case word whose link is otherwise unclear names what is replaced (“… स्थाने”). Not in augment rules (the 6th is the host), not where another word names the part replaced (उपधायाः, एचः), not where no substitute is taught. (Bhāṣya: “सन्देहे नियमः।”)

q: on which stem (aṅga) does it operate?

why.txt: runs on from 6.4.1 (anuvṛtti)

What a suffix was introduced after — a dhātu or prātipadika, with any vikaraṇa or augment added to it — is the aṅga of that suffix. The अङ्गस्य heading (6.4.1) runs to the end of book 7; it names the base, not necessarily the part that changes. (Kāśikā: “यस्मात् प्रत्ययो विधीयते … प्रत्यये परतोऽङ्गसंज्ञं भवति।”)
runs on from 6.4.120 (anuvṛtti)

Where a rule teaches a substitute, a 6th-case word whose link is otherwise unclear names what is replaced (“… स्थाने”). Not in augment rules (the 6th is the host), not where another word names the part replaced (उपधायाः, एचः), not where no substitute is taught. (Bhāṣya: “सन्देहे नियमः।”)

why.txt: runs on from 6.4.134 (anuvṛtti)

q: on which stem (aṅga) does it operate?

why.txt: runs on from 6.4.1 (anuvṛtti)

What a suffix was introduced after — a dhātu or prātipadika, with any vikaraṇa or augment added to it — is the aṅga of that suffix. The अङ्गस्य heading (6.4.1) runs to the end of book 7; it names the base, not necessarily the part that changes. (Kāśikā: “यस्मात् प्रत्ययो विधीयते … प्रत्यये परतोऽङ्गसंज्ञं भवति।”)

Where a rule teaches a substitute, a 6th-case word whose link is otherwise unclear names what is replaced (“… स्थाने”). Not in augment rules (the 6th is the host), not where another word names the part replaced (उपधायाः, एचः), not where no substitute is taught. (Bhāṣya: “सन्देहे नियमः।”)

A 7th-case word naming a following sound, suffix or word (“… परे”) puts the operation on what comes immediately before it. Not a 7th naming a meaning or domain (आर्धधातुके as ‘in its sphere’); if the rule also has a 5th, the 5th wins. (Bhāṣya: “शब्दे सप्तम्या निर्दिष्टे पूर्वस्य कार्यं यथा स्यात्। अर्थे मा भूत्।”)
a 7th-case word naming the setting — “in X” (not “when X follows”)

why.txt: runs on from 6.4.1 (anuvṛtti)

What a suffix was introduced after — a dhātu or prātipadika, with any vikaraṇa or augment added to it — is the aṅga of that suffix. The अङ्गस्य heading (6.4.1) runs to the end of book 7; it names the base, not necessarily the part that changes. (Kāśikā: “यस्मात् प्रत्ययो विधीयते … प्रत्यये परतोऽङ्गसंज्ञं भवति।”)

Where a rule teaches a substitute, a 6th-case word whose link is otherwise unclear names what is replaced (“… स्थाने”). Not in augment rules (the 6th is the host), not where another word names the part replaced (उपधायाः, एचः), not where no substitute is taught. (Bhāṣya: “सन्देहे नियमः।”)

A 7th-case word naming a following sound, suffix or word (“… परे”) puts the operation on what comes immediately before it. Where a rule teaches a substitute, a 6th-case word whose link is otherwise unclear names what is replaced (“… स्थाने”). Not in augment rules (the 6th is the host), not where another word names the part replaced (उपधायाः, एचः), not where no substitute is taught. (Bhāṣya: “सन्देहे नियमः।”)

What a suffix was introduced after — a dhātu or prātipadika, with any vikaraṇa or augment added to it — is the aṅga of that suffix. The अङ्गस्य heading (6.4.1) runs to the end of book 7; it names the base, not necessarily the part that changes. (Kāśikā: “यस्मात् प्रत्ययो विधीयते … प्रत्यये परतोऽङ्गसंज्ञं भवति।”)

why.txt: A 7th-case word naming a following sound, suffix or word (“… परे”) puts the operation on what comes immediately before it. Not a 7th naming a meaning or domain (आर्धधातुके as ‘in its sphere’); if the rule also has a 5th, the 5th wins. (Bhāṣya: “शब्दे सप्तम्या निर्दिष्टे पूर्वस्य कार्यं यथा स्यात्। अर्थे मा भूत्।”)

a qualifier (viśeṣaṇa), agreeing with the word it qualifies (viśeṣya), stands for whatever ENDS in it — so we read “…-अन्त”; only the qualifier, never the qualified word (Nyāsa: “विशेषणेन चतदन्तविधिः [= च तदन्तविधिः], न विशेष्येण”)

Where a rule teaches a substitute, a 6th-case word whose link is otherwise unclear names what is replaced (“… स्थाने”). Not in augment rules (the 6th is the host), not where another word names the part replaced (उपधायाः, एचः), not where no substitute is taught. (Bhāṣya: “सन्देहे नियमः।”)
runs on from 6.4.1 (anuvṛtti)

What a suffix was introduced after — a dhātu or prātipadika, with any vikaraṇa or augment added to it — is the aṅga of that suffix. The अङ्गस्य heading (6.4.1) runs to the end of book 7; it names the base, not necessarily the part that changes. (Kāśikā: “यस्मात् प्रत्ययो विधीयते … प्रत्यये परतोऽङ्गसंज्ञं भवति।”)
runs on from 6.4.144 (anuvṛtti)

A 7th-case word naming a following sound, suffix or word (“… परे”) puts the operation on what comes immediately before it. Not a 7th naming a meaning or domain (आर्धधातुके as ‘in its sphere’); if the rule also has a 5th, the 5th wins. (Bhāṣya: “शब्दे सप्तम्या निर्दिष्टे पूर्वस्य कार्यं यथा स्यात्। अर्थे मा भूत्।”)

q: on which stem (aṅga) does it operate?

why.txt: runs on from 6.4.1 (anuvṛtti)

What a suffix was introduced after — a dhātu or prātipadika, with any vikaraṇa or augment added to it — is the aṅga of that suffix. The अङ्गस्य heading (6.4.1) runs to the end of book 7; it names the base, not necessarily the part that changes. (Kāśikā: “यस्मात् प्रत्ययो विधीयते … प्रत्यये परतोऽङ्गसंज्ञं भवति।”)

Where a rule teaches a substitute, a 6th-case word whose link is otherwise unclear names what is replaced (“… स्थाने”). Not in augment rules (the 6th is the host), not where another word names the part replaced (उपधायाः, एचः), not where no substitute is taught. (Bhāṣya: “सन्देहे नियमः।”)

A 5th-case word of direction (‘after X’) puts the operation on what comes immediately after it — something already there (substitute, augment, elision, accent). Placing a new suffix is 3.1.2; a 5th of cause or ‘other than’, or an explicit पूर्व, is not this rule. (Kāśikā: “पञ्चम्यर्थनिर्देश उत्तरस्यैव कार्यं भवति”)
runs on from 6.4.151 (anuvṛtti)

A 7th-case word naming a following sound, suffix or word (“… परे”) puts the operation on what comes immediately before it. Not a 7th naming a meaning or domain (आर्धधातुके as ‘in its sphere’); if the rule also has a 5th, the 5th wins. (Bhāṣya: “शब्दे सप्तम्या निर्दिष्टे पूर्वस्य कार्यं यथा स्यात्। अर्थे मा भूत्।”)
runs on from 6.4.129 (anuvṛtti)

q: on which stem (aṅga) does it operate?

why.txt: runs on from 6.4.1 (anuvṛtti)

What a suffix was introduced after — a dhātu or prātipadika, with any vikaraṇa or augment added to it — is the aṅga of that suffix. The अङ्गस्य heading (6.4.1) runs to the end of book 7; it names the base, not necessarily the part that changes. (Kāśikā: “यस्मात् प्रत्ययो विधीयते … प्रत्यये परतोऽङ्गसंज्ञं भवति।”)

Where a rule teaches a substitute, a 6th-case word whose link is otherwise unclear names what is replaced (“… स्थाने”). Not in augment rules (the 6th is the host), not where another word names the part replaced (उपधायाः, एचः), not where no substitute is taught. (Bhāṣya: “सन्देहे नियमः।”)

A 5th-case word of direction (‘after X’) puts the operation on what comes immediately after it — something already there (substitute, augment, elision, accent). What a suffix was introduced after — a dhātu or prātipadika, with any vikaraṇa or augment added to it — is the aṅga of that suffix. The अङ्गस्य heading (6.4.1) runs to the end of book 7; it names the base, not necessarily the part that changes. (Kāśikā: “यस्मात् प्रत्ययो विधीयते … प्रत्यये परतोऽङ्गसंज्ञं भवति।”)
आ replaces the first sound of ईयस् after ज्य — SK

Where a rule teaches a substitute, a 6th-case word whose link is otherwise unclear names what is replaced (“… स्थाने”). Not in augment rules (the 6th is the host), not where another word names the part replaced (उपधायाः, एचः), not where no substitute is taught. (Bhāṣya: “सन्देहे नियमः।”)

A 5th-case word of direction (‘after X’) puts the operation on what comes immediately after it — something already there (substitute, augment, elision, accent). Placing a new suffix is 3.1.2; a 5th of cause or ‘other than’, or an explicit पूर्व, is not this rule. (Kāśikā: “पञ्चम्यर्थनिर्देश उत्तरस्यैव कार्यं भवति”)
